_about: INVENTED past jobs for the course prototype, in the shape Omega's job history would take: what was made, how, and what the setters learned. Replace with Omega's real records (King ERP orders plus setters' notes) before any real use.

jobs.part: Stepped pin with collar for a door-lock latch
jobs.notes: Collar cracked at the first trial: moved the collar to station 3 and annealed the wire. Ran 1.2 million a year for 14 years.

jobs.part: Threaded stud M6 with flange for a window regulator
jobs.notes: Flange underfilled until the cut-off length was raised by 0.3 mm. Thread rolled after zinc flake caused galling: roll before coating.

jobs.part: Knurled axle pin for a furniture hinge
jobs.notes: Knurl formed in the header instead of a separate rolling step: saved one operation and 12% of the cost.

jobs.part: Contact pin in brass for a switchgear terminal
jobs.notes: Brass work-hardened in the second blow: slower stroke rate, 150 a minute. Customer measured conductivity on every lot.

jobs.part: Shoulder screw M8 for a seat mechanism
jobs.notes: Long shank bent in transfer: added a guide bush at station 4. Ground the shoulder to h9 after forming.

jobs.part: Rivet pin in stainless steel for an oven door
jobs.notes: Stainless galled the dies: TiCN-coated punches lasted three times longer. Head height kept to 0.5 x diameter.

jobs.part: Hinge axle with groove for window hardware
jobs.notes: Groove turned after forming at first; later formed with a split die, removing the turning step.

jobs.part: Stepped bolt M10 for an instrument panel bracket
jobs.notes: Too heavy for the 4-station header: moved to the 6-station machine. Customer asked for the carbon footprint of each lot.
